about: Clean screenshots of a website, a demo video of it, and screenshots for its web app manifest.

tools.name: take_screenshots
tools.title: Screenshots of a website
tools.asks: screenshots of a site, App Store or Google Play screenshots, Product Hunt gallery images, or a web app manifest's screenshots
tools.description: Opens a website in a headless browser, picks the pages worth showing (home, pricing, features and the like), hides cookie banners, chat bubbles and other floating boxes, and saves desktop, phone and whole-page screenshots in one folder. sheet.png, every page on one picture, is the picture to show first; SCREENSHOTS.md lists each page with why it was picked, its files and its headings. url and page are pages of one public site: a #route, like /app/#/plants, opens that view of a web app, nothing behind a login is reached, and above one page it starts at the site's root. clean hides everything fixed on the screen but a top bar and a side bar, so an app's own tab bar too. iphone is {fact:easyscreenshotkit.size.iphone}, the App Store's 6.9 inch size; mobile is {fact:easyscreenshotkit.size.mobile}, for Google Play phones. For the Google Play feature graphic and Chrome Web Store tiles, use make_launch_stills instead. For a view behind a click, use record_demo_video with steps.

url.description: The website, like https://linear.app, or a page of it. A #route in it, like https://acme.app/app/#/plants, opens that view of the app; another fragment, like #pricing, is left out.

pages.description: How many pages, the home page included (default {default:take_screenshots.pages}). Above 1 the site's root comes first, then url when it is a deeper page, then each page, then pages from the site's menu. With 1, only url and each page are taken, as given; a page that is not of the site stops the run.

page.description: Pages of the same site to take too, like /pricing, or views of a web app by their #route, like /app/#/plants; #/plants alone is that view of url. Each counts toward pages and is taken even past it, and with pages 1 only url and these are taken. Another fragment, like #pricing, is left out.

sizes.description: Any of desktop ({fact:easyscreenshotkit.size.desktop}), mobile ({fact:easyscreenshotkit.size.mobile}, a Google Play phone screenshot), iphone ({fact:easyscreenshotkit.size.iphone}, the App Store's 6.9 inch size), full (the whole page at 1x), mobile-full (the whole phone page at 2x), or WxH from {fact:easyscreenshotkit.custom.side_min} to {fact:easyscreenshotkit.custom.side_max} a side, like 1270x760 for a Product Hunt gallery image. Each takes an optional @scale from {fact:easyscreenshotkit.custom.scale_min} to {fact:easyscreenshotkit.custom.scale_max}, and each size goes in once (default {default:take_screenshots.sizes}).

theme.description: The site's light or dark look, or both, which adds a -dark twin of every picture (default {default:take_screenshots.theme}). A site without a dark theme looks the same in both.

lang.description: The site's version in this language, when it has one: a language code like de, tr or pt-BR.

hide.description: CSS selectors of more elements to hide, like .promo-bar, when something still covers a page.

reduced_motion.description: Ask the site for its reduced-motion version.

clean.description: Set to false to take the pages as they come; hide still hides what it names. Otherwise cookie banners, chat bubbles and everything else fixed on the screen are hidden, except a bar along its top and a tall bar down a side, so an app's own bottom tab bar is hidden too.

pwa.description: Also save screenshots for a web app manifest in pwa/: each page's first screen at {fact:easyscreenshotkit.pwa.wide} and on a phone at {fact:easyscreenshotkit.pwa.narrow}, at most {fact:easyscreenshotkit.pwa.max} in all, checked against Chrome's rules for its richer install dialog, with the manifest entries in pwa/manifest-screenshots.json.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds (default {default:take_screenshots.timeout_seconds}). A run takes two or three minutes, up to five on very long pages, and a slow site can take {fact:easyscreenshotkit.slow_timeout}.
timeout_seconds.hostedDescription: Give up after this many seconds (default {default:take_screenshots.timeout_seconds}). A job here stops after {limit:job_minutes} whatever this says, so more does not help.

done: Show {file:sheet.png} to the user and check that every page needed is there.
For a page that is missing, run again with it in page, and pages above 1: SCREENSHOTS.md lists the pages left out, with why, and others the kit could take.
check_pwa_screenshots with manifest {file:pwa/manifest-screenshots.json} checks the screenshots for a web app manifest.
failed: makersmcp_playbook {topic} lists this tool's errors and their fixes.
A run that fails leaves {folder} as it was, earlier screenshots there too.

done: Show the user the {name:sheet.png} link from the list below and check that every page needed is there.
For a page that is missing, run again with it in page, and pages above 1: SCREENSHOTS.md lists the pages left out, with why, and others the kit could take.
check_pwa_screenshots with manifest {file:pwa/manifest-screenshots.json} checks the screenshots for a web app manifest.
failed: makersmcp_playbook {topic} lists this tool's errors and their fixes.

tools.name: record_demo_video
tools.title: Demo video of a website
tools.asks: a demo video, a walkthrough, a GIF of a site, or footage of the real site for a video
tools.description: Records a short demo video of a website: a tour of the pages worth showing, or the steps in a file. The page plays in a browser window on a backdrop, with a visible pointer, smooth scrolling and a zoom on each click; cookie banners and chat bubbles are hidden, never clicked. Saves demo.mp4 ({fact:easyscreenshotkit.demo.size}, H.264, no sound), demo.gif, poster.png, the picture to show first, and steps.json: each step's start and end, and each click's moment as pressedAt, which music and captions are timed from. A steps file's targets are CSS selectors or text=<words>, and pages and page are for a tour only. A tour gives a page about {fact:easyscreenshotkit.tour.page_seconds} seconds. For still screenshots, use take_screenshots instead.

url.description: The website, like https://linear.app. It replaces a steps file's url line and starts a file whose first step is no visit; a visit to a whole address, as every visit in a tour's demo.yaml, still opens that address.

steps.description: A YAML or JSON file of steps to follow instead of a tour, one action a step: visit, scroll, click, type, key, hover or wait. A target is a CSS selector or text=<words>, and a selector that starts with # goes in quotes. demo.yaml from an earlier tour is one to start from. Not with pages or page.
steps.hostedDescription: A YAML or JSON file of steps to follow instead of a tour, used as it is, like the demo.yaml of a tour an earlier job recorded. One action a step: visit, scroll, click, type, key, hover or wait; a target is a CSS selector or text=<words>. Not with pages or page. Give an https link to the file, or job:<job_id>/<path> for a file an earlier job saved, until the time its result gave.

pages.description: Pages in the tour, the home page included (default {default:record_demo_video.pages}). A page that scrolls takes about {fact:easyscreenshotkit.tour.page_seconds} seconds and one that fits on the screen about {fact:easyscreenshotkit.tour.short_page_seconds}. The tour starts at the site's root and puts pricing last. For a tour only.

page.description: Pages of the same site to take in the tour, like /pricing, or views of a web app by their #route, like /app/#/plants, each taken even past pages. For a tour only.

zoom.description: How far a click zooms in, {bounds:record_demo_video.zoom} (default {default:record_demo_video.zoom}). 1 means no zoom. A step in a steps file can set its own.

background.description: Behind the window, by default a gradient, dark behind a light site and light behind a dark one: a colour like #0f172a, two or three colours for a gradient, or a .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif, .avif or .svg picture file.

frame.description: Set to false for the page alone, filling the video, without the window and the backdrop.

fps.description: Frames a second (default {default:record_demo_video.fps}); steps.json counts its frames at this rate.

theme.description: The site's light or dark look (default {default:record_demo_video.theme}).

lang.description: The site's version in this language, when it has one: a language code like de or pt-BR.

hide.description: CSS selectors of more elements to hide, on top of any under hide in steps.

reduced_motion.description: Ask the site for its reduced-motion version.

clean.description: Set to false to keep the banners and bubbles; hide still hides what it names. Otherwise everything fixed on the screen is hidden but a bar along its top and one down a side, so a step that clicks in an app's bottom tab bar needs this false.

gif.description: Set to false to skip demo.gif, which is made smaller until it is {fact:easyscreenshotkit.demo.gif_max_mb} MB at most.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds (default {default:record_demo_video.timeout_seconds}). A tour looks for more pages only while more than {fact:easyscreenshotkit.tour.pick_seconds} seconds are left, so a short one records the home page, url and each page alone, and a step starts while {fact:easyscreenshotkit.demo.time_left} seconds are left, or a quarter of a shorter run's time.
timeout_seconds.hostedDescription: Give up after this many seconds (default {default:record_demo_video.timeout_seconds}). A job here stops after {limit:job_minutes} whatever this says, so more does not help. A tour looks for more pages only while more than {fact:easyscreenshotkit.tour.pick_seconds} seconds are left, so a short one records the home page, url and each page alone.

done: Show {file:poster.png} to the user before building on the video; it has no sound.
{file:demo.gif} is the same video as a GIF, for a README or a post.
Music, a voice and captions take their times from {file:steps.json}: video.duration is the length and each click's pressedAt its moment.
To change the tour, edit {file:demo.yaml} and record again with it as steps.
failed: makersmcp_playbook {topic} lists this tool's errors and their fixes.
A step that failed is named with its number: check its target against the page, write words as text=<words>, or wait for it first.
A run that fails leaves {folder} as it was, an earlier demo there too.

done: Show the user the {name:poster.png} link from the list below before building on the video; it has no sound.
{name:demo.gif} is the same video as a GIF, for a README or a post.
Music, a voice and captions take their times from {name:steps.json} below: video.duration is the length and each click's pressedAt its moment.
To record this tour again, give steps {file:demo.yaml}; it cannot be changed here.
failed: makersmcp_playbook {topic} lists this tool's errors and their fixes.
A step that failed is named with its number: check its target against the page, write words as text=<words>, or wait for it first.

tools.name: check_pwa_screenshots
tools.title: Check a web app manifest's screenshots
tools.asks: to know whether a web app's install dialog will show screenshots, or a manifest's screenshots checked
tools.description: Checks the screenshots a web app manifest lists against Chrome's rules for its richer install dialog, without a browser: which ones a desktop and a phone would show, and what to fix. A failed check is a normal result, with the report as its summary. It takes a pwa/manifest-screenshots.json from take_screenshots as it is; when the check fails for want of screenshots, take_screenshots with pwa makes ones that pass.

manifest.description: The manifest's file or address, or the site's address, like https://linear.app, when its page links the manifest. A pwa/manifest-screenshots.json from take_screenshots is checked as it is.

passed: Tell the user which screenshots a desktop and a phone will show.
check_failed: Tell the user what the report lists to fix.
take_screenshots with pwa true makes screenshots that meet these rules, with their manifest entries.
